errata.orig:
In a signed proof, the payload is the Merkle Tree root that
corresponds to the log at size tree-size.
errata.correct:
In a signed proof, the payload is the Merkle Tree root that
corresponds to the log at size tree-size. tree-size and leaf-index
are carried in the unprotected header and are not covered by the
signature. Because the same inclusion path can yield the same root
under more than one (tree-size, leaf-index) pair, a verified receipt
authenticates the entry's inclusion under the signed root, but not
its leaf-index or the tree size. A relying party that depends on
either value needs to obtain it from signed data, such as a signed
tree head for the same root and size.
errata.notes:
The signature covers the protected header and the Merkle Tree root;
step 2 of the verification procedure in this section confirms
inclusion. tree-size and leaf-index (Figure 3) are carried in the
vdp of the unprotected header (Figure 5), outside the signature.
Under the algorithm in RFC 9162 Section 2.1.3.2, most receipts still
verify, with the same signature, after only tree-size is changed, and
some after leaf-index is changed along with it. With tree-size held
fixed, no other leaf-index verifies, and the entry cannot be
substituted, so inclusion is unaffected.

Reproduction: https://github.com/AugmentEV/rfc9942-receipt-position
Independently reproduced by Colin Winter (production log,
log.markovianprotocol.com), Laurent Lemonnier (production log,
ts.isoluce.net) and Konrad Gruszka (b7n0de; RFC 9162 trees of up to
64 leaves). An independent implementation, scitt-cose 0.5.0, accepts
both an original and a size-edited receipt. Thanks to Jon Geater for
suggesting errata and to Chris Hopley for implementation experience.
Related text for the CCF receipt profile:
https://github.com/ietf-wg-scitt/draft-ietf-scitt-receipts-ccf-profile/pull/36
Discussed on scitt@ietf.org, November 2026.
Suggested status: Hold for Document Update.

errata.orig:
In a signed consistency proof, the newer Merkle Tree root (proven to
be consistent with an older Merkle Tree root) is a detached payload
and corresponds to the log at size tree-size-2.
errata.correct:
In a signed consistency proof, the newer Merkle Tree root (proven to
be consistent with an older Merkle Tree root) is a detached payload
and corresponds to the log at size tree-size-2. tree-size-1 and
tree-size-2 are carried in the unprotected header and are not
covered by the signature, and the same consistency path can verify
for more than one pair of sizes. A relying party that depends on
either size needs to bind it to the corresponding root through
signed data, such as signed tree heads.
errata.notes:
Here's the §5.3.1 erratum. Section: `5.3.1`. Type: Technical.

Original Text

In a signed consistency proof, the newer Merkle Tree root (proven to
be consistent with an older Merkle Tree root) is a detached payload
and corresponds to the log at size tree-size-2.

Corrected Text

In a signed consistency proof, the newer Merkle Tree root (proven to
be consistent with an older Merkle Tree root) is a detached payload
and corresponds to the log at size tree-size-2. tree-size-1 and
tree-size-2 are carried in the unprotected header and are not
covered by the signature, and the same consistency path can verify
for more than one pair of sizes. A relying party that depends on
either size needs to bind it to the corresponding root through
signed data, such as signed tree heads.


Notes

Companion to the erratum on Section 5.2.1. tree-size-1 and tree-size-2 (Figure 7) are carried in the vdp of the unprotected header; the signature covers the protected header and the newer root only. Under the algorithm in RFC 9162 Section 2.1.4.2, on synthetic trees covering all 2,016 size pairs 1 <= m < n <= 64, 1,984 proofs still verify with only tree-size-2 changed; the 32 exceptions are the pairs (odd m, m+1). With tree-size-2 held fixed, no other tree-size-1 verified. With both sizes changed, every proof verified under another pair, for example (2m, 2n-1), where the verifier does not independently hold the size of the older root. Found by Tiago Pinto and reproduced by the submitter with an independent implementation. Discussed on scitt@ietf.org, November 2026. Suggested status: Hold for Document Update.
